entries.english: Hurry, hurry has no blessing (Haste makes waste)
Slowly, slowly is the way to go (Slow and steady wins the race)
A person is people (No one is an island; humanity is community)
Kindness never rots (A good deed is never lost)
Follow the bees that you may eat honey (Keep good company to prosper)
The curse of the chicken does not bother the kite/hawk
The gratitude of a donkey is kicks
A clear conscience is a soft pillow
The leopard's skin is beautiful to the eyes, but inside is an enemy

entries.english: Whoever earns in the sun eats in the shade (Hard work brings rest)
Whoever wants what is under the bed must stoop for it (No pain, no gain)
If the foundation slopes it has no strength; do not blame the wall when it falls
entries.translation: Msinji ukiinama hauna nguvu; usiushtaki ukuta ukianguka

entries.english: If you make yourself honey, all the flies will eat you
Two roads overcame the hyena (Divided purpose leads to failure)
Where there are many chickens, do not spill millet (Keep confidences discreet)
Better for the eyes to die than the heart to lose hope
entries.translation: Heri kufa macho kuliko kufa moyo

entries.english: The antidote/poison to a word is a word

entries.english: The 8 Historical Swahili Dialect Varieties Documented by Johnston (1919 #21–21g), Burt (1910) & Krapf (1882)
entries.translation: Ki-Ngozi (archaic poetic), Ki-Tikuu / Ki-Bajuni (#21g), Ki-Siu (#21e), Ki-Pate (#21f), Ki-Amu (#21d Lamu), Ki-Mvita (#21c Mombasa), Ki-Unguja (#21 Zanzibar), Ki-Mrima / Ki-Hadimu (#21a)
entries.pronunciation: ki-ngo-zi, ki-ti-kuu, ki-si-u, ki-pa-te, ki-a-mu, ki-mvi-ta, ki-un-gu-ja
entries.context: Sir Harry Johnston (1919, Vol. I, pp. 122–134), Mrs. F. Burt (1910, pp. 1–6), & Dr. L. Krapf (1882)

entries.english: Archaic Kingozi / Kiamu Poetic Vocabulary from 'Hadithi ya Liongo', 'Mashairi ya Liongo' & 'Utumbuizo wa Gungu' (Steere 1870 pp. 439–483)
entries.translation: mjakazi / kijakazi (handmaiden), mbango (wild boar), kikaze (brass vessel), kombe (ceremonial platter), gungu (ancient royal wedding dance), tumbuizo (serenade/ode), utenzi (epic poem), shairi (lyric poem)
entries.context: Bishop Edward Steere (1870) 'Swahili Tales, as Told by Natives of Zanzibar', pp. 439–488

entries.english: 18 Classic Swahili Narratives in Steere's 'Swahili Tales' (1870)
entries.translation: Kisa cha Punda wa Dobi, Sultani Darai, Hekaya ya Mohammadi Mtepetevu, Sultani Majnuni (Nunda mla watu), Mwalimu Goso, Uza Ghali si Uza Rakhisi, Sungura na Simba, Hassibu Karim ad Dini, Ao Rathi ao Mali, Hadithi ya Liongo, Hadithi ya Waridi (Steere 1894)
entries.pronunciation: ha-di-thi ya li-on-go / sul-ta-ni da-ra-i / sul-ta-ni maj-nu-ni
entries.context: Bishop Edward Steere (1870) 'Swahili Tales' & (1894) 'A Handbook of the Swahili Language', Appendix III

entries.english: Kinyume Syllable-Inversion Cipher (Steere 1894 Appendix I, p. 401 & Krapf 1882)
entries.translation: Kinyume (transposing the final syllable to the beginning: e.g., nyumba → mbanyu, kisu → suki, mtu → tumu, njoo → onjo)
entries.context: Bishop Edward Steere & A. C. Madan (1894) 'A Handbook of the Swahili Language', Appendix I, p. 401

entries.english: Traditional Swahili Solar Solar-Agricultural New Year (Nairuz) & 10-Day Decade Counting (Mwongo)
entries.translation: Siku ya Mwaka (Nairuz) & Mwongo (pl. Miongo — 10-day agricultural decades from Mwongo mosi to Mwongo kumi)
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882, p. 255) & Mrs. F. Burt (1910, pp. 166–168)

entries.english: Swahili Mariner's 32-Point Compass, Monsoon Winds & Traditional Weights/Measures (Steere 1894 Appendix V & Burt 1910)
entries.translation: Kaskazi (NE monsoon), Kusi (SW monsoon), Matlai (East), Magharibi (West), Jahazi (dhow); Kibaba (pint measure), Pishi (4 vibaba), Frasila (~35 lbs), Rupia (64 pesa)
entries.pronunciation: kas-ka-zi / ku-si / ki-ba-ba / pi-shi / fra-si-la / ru-pi-a
entries.context: Bishop Edward Steere (1894, pp. 453–458), Mrs. F. Burt (1910, pp. 162–168), & Dr. L. Krapf (1882)

entries.english: The Enclitic Possessive of Alienation/Intimacy (-ngwa: -ngu, -ko, -we) Recorded by Rev. W. E. Taylor (1891 Appendix p. 166)
entries.translation: mamangu, mamako, mamawe (my, thy, his/her mother); babangu, babako, babawe; mwanangu, mwanako, mwanawe; mwenziwe (his companion)
entries.context: Rev. W. E. Taylor (1891) 'African Aphorisms; or, Saws from Swahili-Land', Appendix, p. 166

source: Public Domain Historical Lexicons (Krapf 1850/1882, Steere 1870/1894, Taylor 1891, Madan 1903/1917, Hinde 1904, Burt 1910 & Johnston 1919)
